outcome: Associated maternal complications (abruption, wound infection, eclampsia)
Neonatal complications (transfer to SNCU, intrauterine fetal demise, stillbirth)
cohort: The study included 200 cases of gestational hypertension who were admitted to the Department of Obstetrics and Gynaecology.
finding: The study found that mild pre-eclampsia was the most frequent presentation of gestational hypertension, with 37.6% of participants experiencing maternal morbidity and mortality and significant perinatal complications including transfers to the SNCU, IUFD, and stillbirth.
